request: If edge with bigger radius is considered as top, add supporting structure to the bottom of the frame by offseting inner wall by 2cm with thickness of 0,5cm of the supporting structure all around. This will create step at the bottom of the frame, enlarging bottom surface area. Leave out radii at the bottom edges. Add radii from top, 0,2cm which will create smoothe transition from above. Bottom remains flat.

actions.operation: Define/confirm model orientation such that the side associated with the edge having the bigger existing radius is treated as the top (thereby identifying the bottom as the opposite side).
actions.target: Existing edge(s) that have radii; overall part orientation (top vs bottom).
actions.relational_constraint: Top is the side corresponding to the edge with the bigger radius.
actions.unresolved_reference: The STEP-derived model has large-radius rounds (r≈10) both near the upper and lower Z regions (S7 includes both 'Large top round cylinder' and 'Large bottom round cylinder'), so 'bigger radius' does not uniquely define one side without an explicit datum. For this edit, treat the Z+ edge-round set as TOP and the Z− set as BOTTOM, consistent with the model.json naming of 'top' vs 'bottom' blends/lands.
steps: Inspect the large-radius round faces (Section S7). Use the faces labeled as top rounds as the TOP indicator: 0049 (FACE 42) and corner tori 0042 (FACE 35), 0048 (FACE 41).

Confirm the opposite side as BOTTOM using the bottom-round set: 0045 (FACE 38) and corner tori 0044 (FACE 37), 0046 (FACE 39), plus the bottom planar land faces 0014 (FACE 9) / 0015 (FACE 22) from S5.
Lock the coordinate/datum convention for downstream features: sketch/extrude directions will reference Z+ as TOP and Z− as BOTTOM.

actions.operation: Create a continuous supporting step/ledge feature at the bottom of the frame by offsetting the inner wall profile and forming material with the stated thickness all around.

parameters.offset_direction_definition: Offset the inner opening OUTWARD (toward the outer perimeter) in the X-Z plane to enlarge bottom footprint/contact area; extrude in −Z to form the bottom support thickness.
parameters.feature_behavior: Additive boss/foot ring (continuous all around), merging to existing body.

actions.target: Bottom region of the frame, referenced from the inner wall perimeter/profile.
actions.relational_constraint: Feature is on the bottom of the frame (opposite the identified top) and runs all around (continuous around the full perimeter). Bottom should remain flat.
actions.unresolved_reference: The model shows multiple bottom-region planar faces (0014 and 0015) and multiple blend networks; if the bottom-most datum is not a single planar face, choose the lowest Z planar face among {0014,0015} as the sketch/support reference and ensure the new boss creates the new global bottom plane (flat).
steps: Select the BOTTOM reference plane: pick the lowest-Z planar bottom land face. Prefer 0014 (FACE 9); if 0014 is not the global minimum-Z, use 0015 (FACE 22) instead.
Start a sketch on the chosen bottom land plane (sketch plane parallel to the existing bottom contact region).

Project/convert the inner window opening loop onto the sketch. Use the inner perimeter wall (Section S2) as the geometric source: faces 0006/0007 (inner straight walls) and corner cylinders 0008/0009/0010/0011 define the inner boundary.

Create an offset curve of the projected inner opening by 20 mm (2 cm) OUTWARD (i.e., away from the window opening toward the outer perimeter). Maintain rounded-rectangle topology (straight segments + corner arcs).
Form a closed annular region between: (a) the original projected inner opening loop and (b) the 20 mm outward offset loop. This region is the footprint of the supporting structure.
Extrude (add material) this annular region in the −Z direction by 5 mm (0.5 cm) to create a continuous bottom support ring/step all around. Use 'Join/Add' boolean to merge with the existing body.

Ensure the extrusion creates a single, planar new bottom face for the added structure (flat bottom). If the pre-existing bottom is not the lowest plane everywhere due to blends, allow the new extrusion to define the new global minimum-Z bottom plane for that region.

actions.operation: Remove or avoid applying radii/fillets on the bottom edges of the frame/added supporting step so bottom edges remain sharp.

parameters.bottom_edge_condition: Sharp (R=0) at the new bottom perimeter edges and bottom step edges; remove existing bottom-round faces where they create radiused bottom contact edges.

actions.target: Bottom edges (edges bounding the bottom face and/or bottom of the new step) of the frame/supporting structure.
actions.relational_constraint: No radii at bottom edges; preserve a flat bottom condition.
actions.unresolved_reference: Existing bottom blends include both r≈10 (S7) and r≈2 (S6) faces in the lower Z region; depending on how the original model was constructed, removing them may require either suppressing fillet features (history-based) or delete-face/heal (direct modeling). The exact bottom edge loop after adding the new support will change; ensure all edges lying on the new global minimum-Z plane remain unfilleted.
steps: Identify bottom-edge blend faces currently producing rounded bottom edges: large-radius bottom set in S7: 0045 (FACE 38) plus corner tori 0044 (FACE 37) and 0046 (FACE 39).

Identify small-radius blends in the lower region that may be on/below the bottom lands: S6 faces 0018 (FACE 15), 0019 (FACE 14), 0025 (FACE 16), 0026 (FACE 27), 0027 (FACE 28), 0033 (FACE 26), and the 'lower region' set 0039/0040/0041 (FACE 1/2/3).

History-based workflow (preferred if available): edit the bottom fillet features to exclude all edges that belong to the bottom-most edge loops (edges adjacent to bottom lands 0014/0015 and the new support bottom face). Set bottom fillets to suppressed/removed for these edge sets.

Direct modeling workflow (if no history): use Delete Face (remove blend faces) on the identified bottom blend faces and Heal/Extend to recreate sharp planar/ruled faces between the adjacent surfaces, resulting in crisp intersections at the bottom.

Verify: the entire bottom contact boundary (outer perimeter and the new support perimeter) should meet vertical/side faces with a sharp edge; bottom faces remain planar (flat) with no curvature breaks.

actions.operation: Apply fillets (radii) of the specified size to the top-side edges of the new supporting step to create a smooth transition from above without affecting the bottom.

parameters.fillet_application_rule: Apply only to the upper shoulder edge loop(s) where the new support meets the existing frame; explicitly exclude any edges that lie on the bottom-most (minimum-Z) plane.

actions.target: Top edges of the supporting structure/step (i.e., the edges on the upper side of the added feature where it transitions to the existing frame geometry).
actions.relational_constraint: Fillets are applied from the top side only to smooth the transition from above; bottom remains flat; do not add radii to bottom edges.
actions.unresolved_reference: The specific edge loop(s) to fillet will be created by the new support feature and therefore do not yet have face_code labels in model.json. Limit fillet propagation by selecting only the shoulder edges at the interface between the new step’s top face and its vertical walls (or between the step and the existing bottom land faces 0014/0015), not the new bottom perimeter edges.
target section code: S8 (new supporting step/foot ring section to be created)
steps: After the support extrusion, select the edge loop at the TOP of the new support (the shoulder), i.e., the intersection between the new support’s vertical wall(s) and the existing bottom land face(s) (0014/0015) and/or the underside region adjacent to the inner wall S2.
Apply an edge fillet of radius 2 mm (0.2 cm) to this shoulder edge loop only. Use edge-selection methods that constrain by angle/feature so the fillet stays on the upper transition edges.
Explicitly exclude edges on the new bottom face perimeter (minimum-Z boundary) from the fillet selection so the bottom remains sharp and flat.
Check continuity: confirm the fillet produces a smooth transition when viewed from the TOP direction while the bottom silhouette remains crisp with no radii.

intention: Add a supporting structure at the bottom of the frame.
Create a bottom step to enlarge the bottom surface area.
Maintain a flat bottom while providing a smooth transition from the upper side via small top-side radii.
